title: Michael Fagan and the Invention of Formal Code Inspection (1976)
explainer: Long before pull requests existed, IBM engineer Michael Fagan formalized 'code inspections' - structured, meeting-based reviews with a defined reader, moderator, and rework step - and published the method in the IBM Systems Journal in 1976. His data showed inspections caught far more defects than testing alone, which is the empirical case still cited for why review exists at all. Modern asynchronous PR review is a much lighter-weight descendant of Fagan's rigid process, having kept the core idea (a second pair of eyes before code ships) while dropping the mandatory in-person meeting.
